note: Synthetic data only. The insurer, the policy, the vehicle, the plate and every person named here are invented for this demo. No real policy or customer is represented.

coverages.label: Theft and attempted theft
coverages.inactive_reason: The theft and attempted theft rider was quoted at renewal but was not added to this policy, so a stolen vehicle is not covered.

excluded_drivers.name: Nikos P.
excluded_drivers.reason: Nikos P. is listed as an excluded driver on this policy, so any incident while he is at the wheel falls outside cover.

scenarios.label: Covered collision
scenarios.note: The everyday case. Own damage answers yes and the 250 excess applies.

claim.description: A delivery van reversed into the left front wing while the car was parked. The wing is creased and the door rubs when it opens.

scenarios.label: Theft with no theft rider
scenarios.note: The policy can say no. The rider was never added, so clause TH-7.2 answers for it.

claim.description: The car was taken overnight from outside the house. It was locked and both keys are still with me.

scenarios.label: Glass claim, no excess
scenarios.note: Shows that a deductible of 0 is a real answer and reads differently from no cover at all.

claim.description: A stone thrown up by a lorry chipped the windscreen on the passenger side. The chip has started to spread.

scenarios.label: Excluded driver at the wheel
scenarios.note: Cover exists for the incident but not for this driver. Clause EX-9.1 beats the coverage section.

claim.description: My brother was driving to the shops and clipped a bollard on the passenger side, denting the front door.

scenarios.label: Incident before cover started
scenarios.note: The date decides it. Clause PL-1.2 puts the incident outside the policy period.

claim.description: Someone reversed into the back of the car and left. I only reported it now that I have found the paperwork.

demo_prompts: What does this claim still need from me?
